AGENDA
  ALHAMBRA YOUTH COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  Alhambra Public Library, Learning Center - 101 S. First Street, Alhambra, CA
  91801 Tuesday, July 11, 2023 - 6:00 PM

Commissioners  Members Ex Officio
Daniela Andrade  Michael Macias, Director of Parks & Recreation
Joselyn Cooper  Brie Houghton, Deputy Director
Tatiana Hernandez  Rosalyn Rojas, Recreation Supervisor
Iren Lam
Zachary Oliva
Jason Quach
Natalia Rosales
Andy Tiang
Chen Yu

We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.
If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments
will be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the
Commission on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or
community service, you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised
that the Commission cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on
any item which does not appear on the agenda.
When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

I.  Roll Call
II.  Flag Salute
III.  Approval of the Minutes of the regular meeting of April 11, 2023. Recommended
Action: Approve the minutes of April 11, 2023. *Note: you must have attended the meeting
to vote on the minutes.
 IV.  Staff Report
V.  Oral Communications
VI.  Commission Orals
VII.  Adjournment
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
hereinabove are on file in the Department of Parks & Recreation, Alhambra City Hall, 111 South
First Street, Alhambra, California, and are available for public inspection during regular office
hours which are 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the
meeting described herein, he or she may contact Mr. Michael Macias, Director of Parks &
Recreation, either in person at the Department of Parks & Recreation or by telephone at 626-570-
5044.

Minutes
  Alhambra Youth
  Commission July 11, 2023

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:11 PM on July 11, 2023 at the Alhambra
Civic Center Library, 101 S. 1st St. Alhambra, CA 91801

Commission Members Present: T. Hernandez, I. Lam, M. Gonzalez, N. Rosales and J. Quach

Commission Members Absent: D. Andrade, J. Cooper, Z. Oliva and C. Yu

Also present: Supervisor - R. Rojas and Program Coordinator - F. Reyes

Flag Salute

Approval of Minutes
Commissioner T. Hernandez motioned to approve the Minutes of April 11, 2023. President J. Quach
second the motion.

Staff Report
Supervisor R. Rojas did not have a specific staff report. She did mention the need for projects
for the commission to work on. R. Rojas highlighted the opportunity for the Commission to be
involved with the community during a variety of Summer Programming the City offers. She
also presented the offer of having the Commission work on the concrete signs at ever park in
the city that require a "face-lift".

Supervisor R. Rojas informed the Commission that there is a pre-show at every movie screening
at the Movies at the Park and would inquire about what they entailed. She also stated she
would ask the Community Services Division the need of the Commission to participate at the
Movies in the Park.

Supervisor R. Rojas vocalized how in the previous two months there has not been any
Commissioner present at Tech Talk. She emphasized that sending reminders to the
Commission should improve their attendance. President J. Quach inquired if Commissioner A.
Taing had been present for Tech Talk, however Supervisor R. Rojas confirmed A. Taing's
absence in the last two. Commissioner N. Rosales requested that a list of all the events or
volunteering opportunities be sent to the Commission due to there being new members who
were unaware of the Commissions participation in Tech Talk.

Oral Communications
Commissioner J. Quach stated that participating in these events was a great idea. In the past,
both Commissioners J. Quach and T. Hernandez had participated in City events. J. Quach
mentioned the transition period has affected the Commissions ability to gain traction with the
community. Commissioner J. Quach vocalized the importance of appealing to a younger
demographic by having a games booth at the Summer Movies at the Park.

Commissioner T. Hernandez stated the painting the park signs was a great idea. T. Hernandez
also stated that taking advantage of all the opportunities to be involved with the community
would allow more people to recognized what the Youth Commission offers.
 Program Coordinator F. Reyes highlighted how the Movie Nights are held on Saturdays. He
mentioned the upcoming events that Parks & Recreation will be hosting for the community that
the Commission could be a part of. The events are as follows: Fiesta Alhambra, Pumpkin Run
and the Cheerleading Championships.

Supervisor R. Rojas informed the Commission of how the means of communication with the
Commissioners has shifted to emails and text messages rather than "Group Meet" or phone calls.
She implored the Commission to make an effort to respond to these messages and or emails to
save time for all parties involved.

Commission Orals
President J. Quach commented that the Commission should set clear goals for what is left of the
summer. Commissioner I. Lam stated she was available to attend this upcoming Saturday movie.
Supervisor R. Rojas voiced her appreciation for the enthusiasm to volunteer. However, she
stated it may be best for her to compile a list and contact the necessary parties prior to having
the Commission be present at any City events.

Commissioner T. Hernandez requested a list of the park signs that require more care than others
and to focus on those first. She also echoed her disappointment with the Commission not being
as involved with the community as they previously were. President J. Quach mentioned how the
Commission should work together to build a strong foundation for their future successors. This
would ensure a smoother transition for the future generations of the Youth Commission.
All Commissioners did a brief meet and greet with new Commissioner Marilyn to help her
familiarize herself with her fellow Commissioners as well as City Staff.

Supervisor R. Rojas mentioned how the Recreation Clerk Xavier Moscoso contacts the
Commission via email and text. She stated how the Google # that is used caps the amount of
people on the group message. Commissioner M. Gonzalez requested to be added to the group
message as well. President J. Quach offered to send a text to the commission as well to improved
attendance at meetings as well as communication between members.

Commissioner T. Hernandez noted that most of the Commissioners are also members in service
clubs at their high schools. This would allow them to count the time as community service as
well as getting other members from their service clubs to participate in volunteering with the
Commission.

President J. Quach began giving ideas of what should be done by members prior to their
participation at the Movies at the Park. He recommended making posters, drawings and a flyer
with a QR code that would direct people to the Youth Commission page of the City Website.
